about.intro: Raksha AI helps first-time digital banking users in India check a suspicious SMS, WhatsApp message, UPI request, or call snippet — in their own language — before it costs them money.
about.pipeline1Body: An instant, zero-network keyword/pattern check catches obvious scams first — matters most for low-bandwidth users.
about.pipeline2Body: Your message is turned into a vector via Gemini's free embedding API, so it can be compared against the scam pattern database.
about.pipeline3Body: A vector similarity search against a real database of known scam patterns pulls back the closest matches.
about.pipeline4Body: An LLM (Groq, with Gemini as fallback) judges your actual message — using the retrieved patterns as reference context, not a raw guess.
about.pipeline5Body: Risk score, verdict, the exact flagged phrases, why it matters, and one clear next step — saved only to your own scan history.
about.security1: Every request is verified server-side against the signed JWT — the backend never trusts a client-supplied identity.
about.security2: Row Level Security on every data table — the database itself blocks a user from ever reading another user's scan history, not just the application code.
about.security3: The service role key never leaves the backend; the frontend only ever holds the public anon key, which is safe by design.
about.security4: Rate limiting protects the shared free LLM quota from abuse.
about.security5: If both LLM providers are ever down, the offline rule-engine still returns a conservative result instead of a bare error.
about.stackGroqGemini: primary / fallback LLM, both free tier
about.stackSupabase: Postgres, pgvector, Auth, Row Level Security
about.stackWhisper: hosted speech-to-text for voice/call scans; clips are sent to the provider to transcribe

practice.title: Scam or Safe?
practice.intro: Real (defanged) messages, one at a time. Swipe right — or tap — if you think it's a scam, left if it looks safe. Every answer reveals exactly why, so you leave sharper than you started.

android.rule_generic_warning: This message matches a known scam pattern
android.warning_title: This message looks like a scam
android.scanning_on: On — new messages are checked on this phone
android.scanning_off: Off — no messages are being checked
android.scanning_permission_needed: Raksha needs permission to read incoming messages. They are checked on this phone and never sent anywhere.
android.scanning_permission_denied: Permission refused. You can still check a message by sharing it with Raksha from your messaging app.
android.warnings_blocked_body: Messages are being checked, but notifications are turned off, so Raksha cannot warn you about a scam. Turn on notifications for Raksha.
android.protected_status: Messages are checked and warnings can reach you.
android.scanning_coverage_note: Only SMS is checked. WhatsApp, RCS and other chat apps cannot be read by any third-party app, including this one.
android.shared_clean: No scam pattern found in this message.
android.shared_flagged: This message looks like a scam:
android.shared_hint: Share a message to Raksha from your messaging app to check it.
android.interrupted_body: Android stopped Raksha, so messages that arrived after that were not checked. Checking is running again now.
android.history_empty: No messages checked yet. When a message arrives it will be checked on this phone and appear here.
android.history_disabled: History is turned off, so checked messages are not kept. You can turn it back on in Settings.
android.trace_missing: This record is no longer stored.
android.trace_review_in_service: The patterns for this language are in daily use and have been corrected against real messages.
android.trace_review_inherited: This language uses another language's patterns, because they share a script and much of the same wording.
android.trace_review_unreviewed: The patterns for this language have not yet been read by someone who speaks it. They may miss things.
android.trace_device_only: This check ran on your phone, with no internet. The website's check also compares against a database of known scams and an AI model, which this phone cannot do.
android.settings_history_explainer: Messages you have been warned about are kept on this phone so you can look at them later. They are never sent anywhere.
android.settings_history_on: On — checked messages are kept on this phone
android.settings_clear_confirm_body: This removes every checked message from this phone. It cannot be undone, and you will no longer be able to look back at why something was flagged.
android.settings_storage_note: Stored only on this phone, removed when you uninstall the app. The app cannot send them anywhere — it has no internet permission.
android.call_warning_title: You were warned about this number before
android.call_screening_on: On — callers are checked against messages you were warned about
android.call_screening_off: Off — incoming calls are not checked
android.call_screening_explainer: If someone calls from a number that already sent you a message Raksha warned you about, you get a notice while the phone rings. Calls are never blocked, silenced or recorded, and nothing is sent anywhere.
android.call_screening_unsupported: This phone's version of Android cannot check calls. Message checking still works.
android.call_screening_limitation: Raksha only knows numbers that have already sent you a message it flagged. A caller who has never texted you is not checked, and Raksha cannot hear what anyone says on a call. This warns you about a second contact, not a first.
